subject.title: scope: "shared" sandboxes collapse all agents onto one workspace; no per-agent persona isolation

question: Should shared Docker scope permit agents with distinct persona workspaces, and if so what supported mount and active-workspace contract preserves isolation without breaking shared-container semantics?
rationale: The report presents a potentially severe cross-agent read/write boundary failure, while the safe immediate containment and the intended long-term shared-scope product contract are different decisions.

options.title: Fail closed for distinct workspaces
options.body: Reject or isolate a shared-scope launch when its resolved agent workspace differs from the container’s bound workspace, avoiding cross-agent writes until a supported multi-agent design exists.

options.title: Define multi-agent shared-container mounts
options.body: Support distinct agent workspaces through stable agent-specific paths and an explicitly selected active workspace, with lifecycle, reuse, rw, and ro behavior documented and tested.

options.title: Document same-workspace-only scope
options.body: Define shared scope as valid only for agents intentionally using one common workspace and direct distinct-persona deployments to agent scope.

recommendation.title: Fail closed for distinct workspaces
recommendation.body: Reject or isolate a shared-scope launch when its resolved agent workspace differs from the container’s bound workspace, avoiding cross-agent writes until a supported multi-agent design exists.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete reproduction and can clarify whether the observed deployment relies on intentionally shared container state beyond workspace files.
